title: 拼多多讓年輕人造草莓工廠，170天后“答案”熟了
abstract: 凌晨12點多，呂兆晨又點開了手機裡的監控畫面。 螢幕裡出現了一座佔地50平方米的草莓工廠。 燈光、溫度、溼度、水肥、二氧化碳，草莓生長需要的各種條件，在螢幕上的系統裡都能找到對應按鍵和調節滑塊。 但他盯著螢幕看了10分鐘，最後什麼也沒做成。 之前，草莓工廠建成的那天，他曾帶著一種技術自信走了進去。 “只要感測器足夠多、演算法足夠準，種草莓就是一個參數問題。” 可現實，可能還真不是這樣。 草莓不是標準件 呂兆晨是上海交通大學園藝學專業的一名碩士研究生，這次，他參加了一個有點奇妙的農業比賽。 在這個比賽中，所有進入決賽的隊伍都要從零開始，自行設計建造一座佔地50平方米的植物工廠。 工廠的尺寸是10米×5米×4米。 工廠只能種國產草莓，並且要種6個月。 工廠全程必須採用國產化技術解決方案。 以及，作為一座智慧植物工廠，裝置需要智慧化，能實現無人值守情況下的遠端自主控制。 最後，誰種的草莓品質更好，誰的草莓工廠更可持續發展，誰就贏了。 △四支決賽團隊搭建的草莓工廠 呂兆晨所在的“莓立方”，就是進入決賽的4支團隊之一。 這是一支看起來幾乎沒有短板的隊伍。上海交通大學的師生負責結構設計和環境控制，稷青科技負責工程落地，擁有10年以上草莓種植經驗的嘉興佳莓提供栽培技術支援。 △莓立方團隊合影 呂兆晨自己也有跨學科的背景。本科階段就讀智慧農業專業時，除了傳統農學課程，他還學習了神經網路、深度學習和智慧農機裝備。進入上海交通大學後，他又轉向園藝學研究。 植物和演算法，都懂一些。 入場前，呂兆晨和隊友們心裡多少帶著一些自信。 既然，全密閉的植物工廠能夠完全阻隔自然氣候條件，那麼只要把光、溫、溼、水肥、CO₂全都控制到最適合草莓生長的程度，草莓有什麼理由長不好？ 很快，草莓就給出了第一個反例。在試種階段，草莓出現了 “徒長” 。 所謂“徒長”就是，由於環境失衡，植物會把過多能量用在長莖、長葉上，使得植株非常茂密，但是花和果實的數量卻遠未跟上。 呂兆晨和隊友發現，草莓還真不能總呆在舒適圈，有時候也需要 被“虐” 一下。 所謂虐，其實是 花芽分化誘導 。低溫和短日照會減少草莓體內的開花抑制訊號，讓莖尖從長葉轉向形成花序。反之，如果溫度適宜、水肥充足，草莓就可能繼續把能量用於莖葉生長，遲遲不開花。 團隊由此開始在夜間主動拉大晝夜溫差，模擬季節變化，才終於逼著這批草莓完成花芽分化，抽出花序。 △莓立方植物工廠內，隊長賀世偉在記錄試種 好不容易草莓開花了，負責授粉的熊蜂又來給呂兆晨他們上課了。 近百隻熊蜂被送進工廠後，集體開始“罷工”。它們不肯出巢授粉，有的啃花，有的攻擊工人。 團隊排查到最後才發現，蜂箱恰好被擺在噪音和氣流擾動最強的位置。持續的聲音和風讓熊蜂產生了應激反應。他們只能挪走蜂箱，再給熊蜂留出適應環境的時間。 就這樣，風影響熊蜂，熊蜂影響授粉，授粉決定果實。調節哪一個所謂“參數”，都會沿著生命系統傳導到不知道什麼地方。 為了讓草莓工廠裡的環境儘量均勻，莓立方安裝了110條風道，把經過調節的空氣送到不同種植槽附近，減少上下層和邊緣位置之間的溫溼度差異。 團隊還訓練了兩套影像模型。一套上傳葉片照片就能估算植株體內的氮、鉀含量，為水肥調整提供依據；另一套上傳草莓照片就能預測糖度、酸度和糖酸比。部分指標的驗證精度達到90%左右。 有一次，草莓葉片邊緣出現焦黃。年輕隊員調取影像和環境記錄，準備交給模型分析。團隊裡的種植專家看了一眼，3秒就判斷出了問題。 老師傅不懂什麼參數，但他多年來看了成千上萬個葉片的顏色、捲曲程度和整株狀態，已連成一個整體。呂兆晨說， 他們就是想把這樣的“手感”捏進模型裡。 到了8月上旬，莓立方迎來第一批夏季草莓。團隊共採收295顆，平均單果重超過20克，最大一顆超過40克，並在由普通消費者擔當評委的大眾品鑑活動中取得第二名。 △呂兆晨在終期評審現場，介紹團隊種植成果 但此後的長週期執行又提出了新的問題。後續種植過程中，現場操作人員與種植專家之間的溝通不夠順暢，部分農事判斷沒有及時落實，“草莓這個東西很難種，只要一株有問題，它有可能傳染其他株”——莓立方最終獲得了第三名。 “以前做研究，失敗可以重來。但這次是一株一株活著的草莓在承擔我們判斷的後果，這種責任感是實驗室裡學不到的。”呂兆晨說。 在青藏高原上種菜 這已經是多多農研科技大賽舉辦的第五屆了。 這項由拼多多發起的農業科技創新大賽，每一屆考題都不相同，比如第一屆是在雲南高原種草莓，第二屆種番茄，第三屆在集裝箱內種生菜，第四屆不僅要種，還要自己從零設計整個集裝箱植物工廠。 大約兩年前，上海小夥、海歸IT男秦楚漢走進了第四屆決賽的現場， 最終以“優勝獎”告終。 走出賽場的他手裡攥著一張紙，上面密密麻麻記了一二十個問題。那是評委對他們植物工廠生菜種植整體方案提出的意見和建議。 據他覆盤，他和團隊太想把前沿技術和概念全塞進這個植物工廠了，結果反而是1+1<2。比如團隊原本引以為傲的多光譜大功率LED燈，提供的光照已經超過植物光合作用能夠利用的上限。多出來的能量沒長成更多蔬菜，只變成了電費。 失望是肯定有的，秦楚漢當時不是第一次造植物工廠了，他16歲赴加拿大留學，又從經濟學轉入計算機專業，做人工智慧和機械控制。2016年前後，他就在加拿大搭起植物工廠，用演算法控制作物生長，積累了較為成熟的技術路線。 於是比賽結束了，秦楚漢的植物工廠種菜夢也開始了。 2025年1月，西藏日喀則定日縣發生6.8級地震，迅速攫住了秦楚漢的目光。 當時他在群裡看到募捐號召，便和團隊商量著能為災區做點什麼，最後決定把植物工廠的裝置和技術送過去，讓當地人以後也能吃上新鮮蔬菜。 讓一輛小汽車進藏就已經很艱難了，可想而知，一座座植物工廠呢？從上海開大貨車去亞東縣，路況不好時要走10天以上；運送植物工廠的過程中有兩輛卡車半路拋錨，其中一輛直接發動機報廢，只能再叫一輛大車把它揹回去。 幾個月後，新的植物工廠終於被運到了上海市普陀區對口支援的 日喀則市亞東縣。 到西藏的第二天，秦楚漢就感覺自己的臉曬黑了。海拔高、紫外線強，稍不注意就會曬傷。朋友看到他也開玩笑說，像是“換了個人種”。 在高原上，舉步維艱。字面意義上的步伐，以及——植物工廠的營造步伐。 秦楚漢最深刻的感悟，就是 學會敬畏和放慢腳步。 亞東縣平均海拔3500米。稍微走快一點就上氣不接下氣。秦楚漢還得了肺水腫，只能回上海養病，等養好了又重新趕回西藏。 從那以後，他時刻告誡自己：凡事不要急，慢慢來。 為了防止感冒加重高反，他學會了“三明治穿衣法”，每天都是徒步穿搭；為了記錄海拔、心肺和血氧等指標，他還自己手搓了一個App。 初到西藏，沒有住的地方，秦楚漢乾脆在植物工廠裡住了整整一個月。這裡沒有暖氣，也沒有廁所。這種條件下克服身體不適已著實不易，但植物工廠還要開工——這些裝置，對於沒有配套技術的當地人而言，無異於一堆廢鐵。 於是團隊幾個人又開始上海、西藏兩頭跑，在當地招員工，從零開始培養新農人。 不僅僅是缺人，海拔一高，裝置運作的環境也大變特變了。 於是平原上的成熟方案搬到高原，瞬間又會變成實驗方案。 高原地區氣壓低、空氣浮力小、紫外線強，很多習以為常的規律不再奏效，比如空調等裝置老化極快，比如塌方或電網檢修導致的停電時有發生……生產程序隨時會被打斷。 但青藏高原也有它得天獨厚的優勢。這裡綠色能源極其豐富，最低電價只要兩毛錢一度；而喜馬拉雅南麓的河谷地帶常年多雨、缺乏日照和耕地，恰好放大了植物工廠佔地少、不受氣候影響的長處。 生活在亞東縣的老百姓，近十年才吃上葉菜。本地集市上賣的葉菜大多從四川、雲南長途轉運過來，不僅價格高，新鮮度也大打折扣。 秦楚漢還記得，第一次把植物工廠運過去時，裡面空蕩蕩的什麼都沒有，十幾個附近的村民探頭探腦地往裡看，一邊看一邊開著玩笑，既好奇又開心。 迄今為止，他們已經往高原運送了13個植物工廠，試種過芽苗菜、生菜、小青菜、菌菇等10餘個品種，一個月產量能達到6000斤，價格也比外地運來的更便宜。 如今，當地居民已經能隨時吃上新鮮的芽苗菜，甚至用這些菜包起了菜包子， 飲食習慣都發生了改變。 兩年前那張攥在手裡的紙上，密密麻麻的問號已不在，取而代之的全是篤定的勾。 用技術和植物對話 第五屆多多農研科技大賽，一支由中國農業大學碩博生組成的團隊“賽博農人”蟬聯了一等獎，這已經是這支隊伍第五次參賽。 △賽博農人隊員相互分享獲獎的喜悅 賽制上，大賽使用的是雙重檢驗。大眾評審負責嘗草莓，直接去品草莓的甜度、香氣和口感；專家評審則負責審視這套方案，能否在商業世界裡持續執行。 儘管這次“賽博農人”的隊員們此前沒有實際的草莓種植經驗，但在草莓苗被移栽進植物工廠的113天后，團隊迎來了第一次採收。 此後的50天裡，他們在126平方米的栽培面積內，累計收穫284.45公斤“粉玉2號”草莓，最大單果重達73.7克。 不僅拿下了賽事一等獎，還在大眾評審中位列第一。 △大眾評審環節用賽事成果做的草莓甜品 具體而言，他們提出了一套以“與植物對話”為核心的智慧環控方案。 所謂“與植物對話”，核心是“以植物為本”。在他們的系統裡，整座植物工廠成為了一個大型同化箱。系統通過監測內部的淨二氧化碳交換量、收集空調除溼的冷凝水 來計算植株群體的光合作用與蒸騰作用， 再配合相機監測葉片的生長動態。 這些即時指標反饋給AI演算法後，系統會在生長策略庫裡自動尋優，動態調節光、溫、溼和水肥。 “軟硬體做得再好，只要病蟲害不能防控住，什麼都是白搭。最終還是用植物檢驗……植物才能判斷我們的軟硬體的好壞。”大賽評委、中國農業大學水利與土木工程學院教授賀冬仙在點評時直言。 近兩年，歐美垂直農業經歷了高達百分之八九十的倒閉與重組潮。為什麼資本和最前沿的硬體堆不出健康的產業？ 獲得本屆大賽二等獎的“擬生態”團隊成員何朝輝說， “一個重要原因就是過於強調技術，過度關注工業技術的應用，卻忽視了種植本身。” △“擬生態”團隊成員何朝輝 “種植就是種植，草莓就是草莓。無論是工業技術還是現在所謂的AI，都應該發揮輔助作用，幫助提升種植水平，而不能把技術本身當成核心目標。如果只強調工業技術，而忽視植物的生長規律，這個方向就是錯誤的。” 這也和賽事理念相承，用“結果”說話，讓植物來檢驗方案。 作為賽事主辦方的拼多多，通過“千億扶持”計劃加大科創投入，以賽事為抓手，為這群年輕人提供了一塊幾乎“無限自由”的試驗田。 “從零開始搭建一座植物工廠，整個過程給了我們極高的自由度，植物工廠完全由我們自主設計、自主建造、自主運營，拼多多這邊完全不加任何干預，我們可以盡情發揮自己的創意，將實驗室裡的一些理論知識運用到實際生產當中。”呂兆晨說。 “參加比賽之前，我一直以為做農業的人不多，或者說與我同齡的人不多。” 呂兆晨感慨，在上海交大做農業的人本來就少，願意從事植物工廠研究的更少；但在賽場上看到“賽博農人”等團隊裡那麼多和自己年紀相仿的同齡人，對他來說是一種很大的鼓舞。 “我們不是一個很龐大的群體，但至少還有人。能在這條路上找到結伴同行的人，是非常重要的。” 一顆草莓，就這樣，給一群年輕的科研人上了一堂關於技術、經驗和生命的課。 在多多農研科技大賽的草莓工廠，新農人們必須要投入實幹，拿出果子和賬本了。 畢竟這場賽事最後比的不是商業PPT的完成度和頁數，種植成果、工廠設計與建設、成本和能耗才是大頭。 “你們怎麼去控制畸形率？” “至少要做到多大面積才可能賺錢？” “別隻講防病原則，實際發生過什麼病？最後怎麼處理的？” “你們草莓的糖度、糖酸比、硬度、香氣和光澤能支撐溢價嗎？” 或許，當最終評審的問題和標準變得越來越接地氣的時候，這場比賽才算真正落到實處了。

title: How public sector organizations can govern AI at scale
abstract: • Unity Gateway provides clear answers on cost, compliance, and data residency let public sector teams move AI projects forward. • Agencies already using Unity Catalog can govern AI the same way they govern data, controlling model access, capping spend, and tracking every request. • Databricks manages data residency for its hosted models by geography, giving compliance teams a documented answer on where AI requests are processed. Every government CIO has the same mandate right now: adopt AI, move faster, do more with less. Coding assistants are making development teams more productive. Agents leveraging large language models are opening up new ways to serve citizens. And the organizations that don't move on AI risk falling behind. But public sector organizations operate in a different reality than commercial enterprises. Before a single AI model or agent gets called, someone has to answer a set of questions that most AI tools or inference providers weren't designed to address. It’s not that public sector organizations are slow to adopt technology, but the stakes are just different. These organizations handle citizen data, defense information, law enforcement records, and public funds. The governance requirements that come with that responsibility are not optional. Until recently, meeting those requirements meant saying no to AI, or at least saying "not yet." The tools available didn't give governance, budget, and compliance teams what they needed to say yes. Here's what it looks like on the ground. A digital services team at a public sector organization starts using third-party coding agents, such as Codex and Claude Code, to help developers work faster. Developers love them, but then come the governance questions: Who has access to which models? Why is AI spend climbing so fast? The compliance team asks where the data is going. It turns out the third-party coding agent platform is routing requests to infrastructure in another country. For an organization handling sensitive operational data, that's a problem. The budget office asks about costs. No one can say how much the tools are costing or which teams are driving the spend. Response times are slow and unnecessary tokens are being used because requests are traversing infrastructure that was never optimized for the use case. The result is predictable: the compliance team can't sign off, the budget office can't plan for it, and the AI project stalls. Not because teams don’t need AI, but because no one can answer the basic governance questions. This pattern repeats across agencies and geographies. The specific regulations vary, whether it's GDPR, FedRAMP, or national sovereignty frameworks, but the underlying dynamic is the same. Teams want to use AI. Governance teams want to say yes. But the tools in the middle aren't giving either side what they need. The public sector organizations that are making real progress on AI share a common trait: they solved governance before they scaled adoption. They didn't bypass the governance questions. They found a way to answer them centrally, so every team didn't have to figure it out on their own. That's the role Unity Gateway plays within Databricks. No single model fits every mission, so agencies need choice. Choose one model for all three, and the agency either overpays for routine questions or under-serves its most demanding work. Governance has to make room for the right model for each mission while keeping data, users, and budgets under control. What Unity Gateway gives governance and budget teams is straightforward. The organization controls which AI models, coding agents, MCPs, and AI tools are available and to whom. Teams get day-zero access to the latest frontier and open-source models, while administrators decide which models to enable and who can use them. New models don't become available to every user by default. For example, at a revenue agency, that means an investigations unit can use AI on taxpayer records while access stays limited to the investigators authorized to work those cases. Spending limits and hard caps can be set by user, team, or use case, and every request is tracked and attributable. Compliance policies, including content guardrails and access controls, apply at the platform level to every AI interaction, regardless of which team or application initiates it. Beyond setting spending limits, Unity Gateway helps organizations reduce AI costs with Smart Routing , which directs tasks to more cost-effective models while maintaining quality. For an agency modernizing legacy systems on a fixed budget, that means routine coding tasks go to lower-cost models, stretching the budget further without slowing developers down. For organizations with strict data residency requirements, governance also has to cover where AI requests are processed. A national health service applying AI to patient records, for example, has to be able to show regulators where that data goes. Databricks manages data residency for its hosted foundation models by geography, and account admins can require that these requests be processed within their workspace's geography. Compliance teams get a clear, documented answer on where those requests are processed. And because Unity Gateway supports models from multiple providers, open-source models, and external endpoints, teams aren't locked into a single vendor. They can use the best model for each task, while the governance team retains full visibility. When organizations move their AI workloads to Unity Gateway, the dynamic that was stalling adoption reverses. Developers get access to the models they want through Databricks' infrastructure without each team needing to self-govern. The governance team gets a single view of AI activity across models, agents, and tools, with unified traces that capture requests, token usage, costs, and tool activity. For the benefits agency, that means leaders can see that AI tools for processing claims are being used heavily and at a reasonable cost, so they can expand those tools to more caseworkers and get benefits to people faster. The governance requirements that were blocking AI adoption become the unified foundation that makes it possible. When the compliance team has confidence that AI usage is visible and managed, and the budget office can see exactly where spending is going, saying yes to AI gets much easier. Governments around the world are investing in AI while tightening data protection and sovereignty requirements. From citizen services to national security, the agencies that move fastest will be the ones that can match each mission to the right model, with the right controls. Unity Gateway is how Databricks helps public sector organizations get there. It meets agencies where they are, with existing data governance in place, and adds AI governance on top. No parallel system. No multi-year implementation. Just the controls that public sector leaders need to move forward. Do we need new infrastructure? No. Unity Gateway is built into Databricks, allowing organizations to centrally manage AI access, security, and costs without deploying or maintaining a separate AI gateway or AI governance solution. Can we control which models our teams use? Yes. While Unity Gateway provides day-zero access to the latest AI models, administrators can control which models are enabled and who can use them. Organizations can approve models and manage access by user, group, or team, so teams can adopt new AI capabilities without compromising governance. Yes. Budgets and hard spending caps can be set by user, team, or use case. Every request is tracked. Does this work with multiple model providers? Yes. Unity Gateway supports models from multiple frontier model providers, open-source models, and external endpoints. Can we keep AI processing within our geography? Yes. Account admins can require that requests to Databricks-hosted foundation models be processed within their workspace's geography.

title: Real-time fraud detection with Feature Views
abstract: Real-time fraud detection depends on three kinds of features: what a customer did seconds ago, how they normally spend and how the current payment compares. Those features have to be computed the same way for model training and for live scoring — otherwise data leakage and training-serving skew quietly erode model quality. Feature Views, part of Databricks Feature Store, address this. You define each feature once, and that definition produces both point-in-time training data and the managed pipelines for online inference. A $900 payment may be routine for one customer and unusual for another. When it arrives, a fraud model has only a moment to decide whether it looks normal, needs review or should be blocked. Approving a fraudulent transaction can cost the customer money. Blocking a legitimate one disrupts their payment experience and erodes their trust in the platform. The transaction alone doesn't tell the whole story. The model also needs to know how this customer normally transacts and what they did seconds, minutes, days or weeks ago. During training, features must use only information available when each payment occurred. During live scoring, they must reflect recent transactions quickly enough to catch suspicious activity. If the two paths implement the logic separately, small differences between them creep in. This walkthrough follows that $900 payment from a Kafka stream to a fraud score served by Model Serving, with code at each step. The central idea is that one feature definition, driving both training and serving, gives you point-in-time correct training data and consistent online features. You don't build a separate pipeline for each path. A Feature View is a Databricks Feature Store definition that specifies a feature's source, entity keys, time semantics and transformation. The same definition computes historical values for training and drives the managed pipelines that keep features fresh for serving. One API covers batch, streaming and on-demand features. Unity Catalog governs their definitions, permissions and lineage. Two failure modes motivate this design: Feature Views bring streaming feature computation into the same data science workflow as historical training and live scoring. You can evaluate features against past transactions, then use the same definitions to keep customer context fresh for live decisions. The goal is to flag suspicious payments as they arrive without raising false alarms on legitimate ones. On its own, the $900 payment may look harmless. But if it's the 10th payment in five minutes, it could be part of a suspicious burst. Any delay in recognizing that burst gives someone with access to a compromised account more time to make additional payments. A Fraud Detection application built with Databricks Apps processes a stream of financial transactions. Each event includes a customer ID, amount, payment type, timestamp and origin and destination countries. The application sends each transaction to a Model Serving endpoint. It then displays the transaction's risk score alongside live transaction volume, flagged transactions and country-to-country flows. The model combines three kinds of context: The architecture has a historical path for training and an online path for inference. Both start from the same feature definitions in Unity Catalog. The historical path reads the Stream's ingestion table to build point-in-time training sets. The online path materializes aggregates to the Online Feature Store, where Model Serving reads them at request time. Before deciding which features to serve, you can test alternatives against historical transactions. Does a five-minute transaction count give a stronger signal than a 15-minute count? Does comparing the current amount with the customer's spending variability help beyond using their average alone? In this example, customer transaction events arrive as Kafka streams. A registered Stream holds the connection, schema and ingestion settings, and a StreamSource references it to compute real-time features. Kafka topics don't retain enough history for model training. Databricks therefore manages an offline copy of the stream in an ingestion table. For training or backfilling an online store, Databricks calculates historical values from the ingestion table and uses the live Kafka feed for the most recent data. On ingest, transformation_sql reshapes nested fields from the Kafka value payload into the schema the features need. The projection becomes part of the source definition, so you don't deploy a separate preprocessing pipeline. For our payment, the Kafka value payload contains: The demo uses demo_user_id alongside customer_id to keep the customer histories of different app users separate. We define the five-minute count with RollingWindow . The companion notebook includes imports, configuration, and the full source projection. You can inspect its historical values in a notebook with compute_features(features=[recent_transaction_count]) . The 10-minute total uses the same source and keys, with Sum over a 10-minute RollingWindow. A Sawtooth window is a long-lookback aggregation whose oldest boundary advances in daily steps. It combines batch-computed history with streaming updates for recent activity. For our $900 payment, SawtoothWindow adds a 30-day spending baseline to the short rolling windows. Both kinds of window keep recent activity fresh. Because the Sawtooth window's oldest boundary moves daily rather than continuously, its effective lookback is slightly longer than 30 days. The baseline uses the built-in Avg , StddevPop and Count aggregations on payment amounts over the same Sawtooth window. Databricks starts a managed ingestion pipeline when a Stream is created and keeps incoming events in its ingestion table. If you also need events from before the Stream existed, StreamBackfillSource lets you supply your own history during Stream setup. Once the table covers the full lookback, a new Sawtooth feature can use it right away instead of waiting 30 days for events to accumulate. An on-demand feature is computed at request time by combining values from the scoring request with stored features. Comparing a live transaction against a customer's historical baseline is a common way to spot abnormal behavior. In Feature Views, inference-time information is represented with a RequestSource — here, transaction_amount from the application's request. Two customers can both average $300 per payment but spend very differently. With standard deviations of $100 and $600, the same $900 payment sits six standard deviations above one customer's average and only one above the other's. The model combines this comparison with recent activity and payment details to estimate fraud risk. The Sawtooth aggregations maintain the 30-day average and standard deviation. The on-demand feature combines them with the current amount to calculate (current_amount - average) / standard_deviation . We implement this calculation as a Python UDF registered in Unity Catalog: The feature definition uses registered upstream Feature objects. FeatureViewSource brings together the current amount and the three 30-day statistics, and CustomUDF invokes the function: When there isn't enough usable history, the function returns zero as a fallback. A separate indicator lets the model tell that fallback apart from a true zero, which means the payment matches the customer's average. The same derived feature is evaluated against historical inputs during training, and against the current request plus retrieved statistics during inference. During feature development, you can inspect feature definitions in a notebook with compute_features() . This works for derived features whose inputs come entirely from historical source data. For request-dependent comparisons such as amount_deviation , use create_training_set() instead, which supplies the current payment fields from labeled examples.

title: Chicago’s bid to lead the country in quantum computing
abstract: Chicago’s bid to lead the country in quantum computing New IBM Quantum System Two supports Illinois’ place at the center of the American quantum computing industry. Date 6 Nov 2026 Authors Rafi Letzter Topics Network Community Systems Share this blog Was this blog post helpful? Yes No Key Takeaways: IBM has deployed an IBM Quantum System Two with an IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor at the University of Chicago's Hyde Park Labs to support the National Quantum Algorithm Center (NQAC) and the wider Illinois quantum ecosystem. IBM is an anchor partner of the NQAC in Chicago, which was created by the State of Illinois in concert with the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP). IQMP will be a quantum computing campus on the former US Steel South Works site on Chicago's Southeast Side, and will eventually house the new computer and NQAC. The IBM Quantum System Two sits at street level behind floor-to-ceiling windows at Hyde Park Labs on 53rd Street. IQMP CEO Harley T. Johnson calls it "probably the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world." The University of Illinois, University of Chicago, and other key research and business institutions in the region are already conducting important research that advances quantum computing as a technology, science, and industry. Johnson and Mason emphasize that Illinois' quantum leadership is rooted in decades of investment in scientific and engineering talent. Across the Midwest, universities, national laboratories, and technology companies have helped develop generations of researchers, engineers, and entrepreneurs. Harley T. Johnson wants Chicago to be the Silicon Valley of quantum computing. Johnson is a professor of mechanical science and engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (U of I.) and CEO of the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park (IQMP). He is part of a cohort of leaders spanning academia, government, and industry who are working to establish Chicago as the hub of America’s quantum computing industry. That effort has a physical center. With a $500 million investment from the state of Illinois under Governor JB Pritzker, as well as support from IBM, U of I., the University of Chicago, and other partner organizations, the IQMP will be a massive campus on a pier that once housed a U.S. Steel South Works plant on Chicago’s Southeast Side. As part of that project, the state established the National Quantum Algorithm Center (NQAC), a Chicago-based collaborative initiative focused on advancing quantum algorithms and applications to support the emerging quantum computing industry. IBM is an anchor partner. To support the algorithm center and surrounding quantum ecosystem, IBM has unveiled a newly installed IBM Quantum System Two with an IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor at UChicago’s Hyde Park Labs. The system will operate at UChicago before eventually relocating to the IQMP campus, which will serve as the long-term home of both the NQAC and the new quantum computer. Pritzker and Johnson joined a group of Illinois leaders for the ribbon cutting including UChicago President Paul Alivisatos, Chairman of the Illinois Economic Development Corporation John Atkinson, Assistant Director and Chief Workforce Officer of the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity Stacia Edwards, P33 CEO Brad Henderson, U of I. Chancellor Charles Isbell, and UChicago Vice President of Research Nadya Mason. IBM Director of Research Jay Gambetta, and Director of Quantum Algorithm Centers Hanhee Paik stood with them to unveil the quantum computer at a ceremony on November 6. Mason has been a researcher and leader in the quantum field for decades and has played a key role in building Chicago’s quantum ecosystem. She said that the arrival of the IBM Quantum System Two will accelerate the work and increase the excitement for quantum computing that’s already taken root in the region. Johnson said it’s important to him that the computer will have such a prominent location in the city. “It’s probably the most publicly visible quantum computer in the world,” Johnson said. Sitting at ground level behind floor-to-ceiling windows at Hyde Park Labs on 53rd Street, the mirrored panels of the IBM Quantum System Two will reflect the faces of students from the public high school just a block away as they walk past and peer through the glass. "Imagine getting to say, ‘My daughter goes to school every day and passes a real quantum computer.’ That’s mind blowing,” Johnson said. Already, Mason said, adults are getting inspired by the possibilities the new quantum computer represents. “For our graduate students, having access to a quantum computer is incredible,” she said. There are many students and researchers in the Pritzker School of Engineering at UChicago with deep expertise in quantum information science and engineering. But in the lead up to the ribbon cutting, Mason said she’s received questions from professors and administrators in physics, other fields of engineering, and even fields like medicine, all interested in applying quantum to their own domains. The presence of a leading quantum computer in such a public place is a powerful source of inspiration as well as a practical tool. The IBM Quantum System Two is new, but Illinois’ quantum momentum isn’t Paik compared the coalition driving quantum computing in Illinois to “the Avengers”—super-heroes working together to achieve great collective goals. Organizations including the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity, the University of Chicago, the University of Illinois, the Chicago Quantum Exchange, the Chicago technology and innovation hub P33, and the Illinois Economic Development Corporation have spent years building the foundations for what is now emerging on Chicago's South Side. Paik noted that numerous leaders, including Johnson and Mason, have helped make this progress possible, and highlighted Governor Pritzker's leadership as instrumental to the effort's success. The region is also home to important quantum computing research. In 2026, a joint team from the University of Chicago and IBM demonstrated quantum advantage on a structured computational task, offering an alternative to traditional random circuit sampling benchmarks. Running on an IBM quantum system, the experiment leveraged 70 logical qubits to complete a calculation in approximately 15 minutes, surpassing the practical capabilities of today's leading classical simulation methods while providing a built-in mechanism for verification. Illinois is also advancing the convergence of quantum and high-performance computing (HPC). Researchers at U of I., the National Center for Supercomputing Applications (NCSA), and IBM integrated NCSA's DeltaAI supercomputer with an IBM Quantum system, bringing quantum-centric supercomputing capabilities to the state. Following the announcement of the expanded collaboration in April 2026 , the joint team delivered its first demonstration within six months: a computation of Cu₃C₆O₆, a strongly correlated kagome-lattice metal, using the integrated DeltaAI and IBM Quantum systems. The results will be presented at SC26 in November, highlighting the pace of innovation enabled by this collaboration. Beyond these scientific and technical advances, Illinois is increasingly focused on translating quantum innovation into real-world impact. The NQAC plays a key role in this effort, bringing together industry, academic, and government partners to develop quantum-enabled solutions for meaningful business and societal challenges. Through the NQAC Grand Challenge program , member organizations are exploring applications across sectors including drug discovery, advanced manufacturing, energy, finance, and logistics. The accomplishments highlighted above represent only a snapshot of the innovation taking place across Illinois.

title: “Does Meta think we can’t read?” Meta abandons sketchy commercial terms update.
abstract: After weeks of backlash —and a failed attempt to quell it —Meta has indefinitely delayed plans to update its commercial terms and require Meta Business account users to allow extensive AI training on external websites linked on Facebook. “We’re pausing the ‌changes ⁠as we continue to engage with stakeholders and ​take ​our ⁠time to get this right. ​In the ​meantime, ⁠our existing terms remain in ⁠effect,” a Meta spokesperson told Reuters. Soon after Meta notified business account holders of the upcoming changes, legal experts warned Nieman Lab that the vague language could allow the company to ignore scraping preferences specified in robots.txt files and exhaustively crawl vast amounts of off-Facebook content for AI training. Since virtually every news publisher has a Facebook page, Nieman Lab sounded the alarm that Meta could potentially avoid millions in licensing fees if the TOS update happened as planned. Ars broke down the changes after Meta announced them, noting that businesses—including news publishers involved in drawn-out legal battles over unwanted AI scraping—had no way to opt out. To keep a business Facebook page, they had to allow Meta to crawl any linked external sites. The terms even required publishers to create test credentials so Meta’s bots could reliably bypass paywalls. Meta faced global scrutiny The changes were initially supposed to take effect on October 30. But Meta pushed that date back to November 20 amid pushback from Facebook users, courts, and regulators around the world. Courts in Brazil and Norway issued preliminary injunctions blocking the terms after organizations in those countries promptly filed lawsuits, Nieman Lab reported . The United Kingdom’s Competition and Markets Authority also opened a formal investigation into whether Meta was exploiting a dominant position to seize valuable AI training data. In a LinkedIn post , Theo Bamber, chief executive of the UK’s News Media Association, pointed to “the continued arrogance of this company to think everyone will just be OK with its actions” as “staggering.”

title: Could potential AI clones of GTA VI force a quicker official port?
abstract: Yesterday, when reporting on emerging efforts to pipe the console version of GTA VI through a PC's DLSS-powered Nvidia GPU , we mentioned in passing that PC players could instead just wait for the AI-assisted decompilation port that will no doubt be coming in short order. Now, a former Rockstar tech director says he thinks that exact threat could cause the developer to work faster on the official PC version of its soon-to-release crime/lifestyle simulator. Obbe Vermeij hasn't worked at Rockstar since 2009 , but in a new interview with Rock Paper Shotgun , he recalled how artists for the PC version of the original top-down Grand Theft Auto were incensed when the console version squashed the game's 256-color textures down to 16 colors for the PS1 release. "So it always has been that sort of awkward relationship between PC and the console," Vermeij said. "So in those days, it was like PC first and then console second, even though that didn't really make much sense for the sales, because the PlayStation versions sold way better."

title: GPT-6 Astra Covertly Underperforms on Safety Research Tasks
abstract: For a while, UK AISI , Redwood Research and others have been concerned specifically with the possibility that AIs would sabotage safety research, and have invested in looking for signs that this may be happening. This was also a key element in AI 2027 , and in many threat models of how the future goes badly. It is easy to understand why this form of misalignment could be uniquely dangerous. Differentially sabotaging safety research could preserve and expand misalignment through model generations in escalating fashion, with fatal consequences. A misaligned AI could ensure a misaligned successor. It is also easy to understand why this is an extremely alarming thing to discover, even if the particular example or model involved is not directly dangerous. Silently and differentially sabotaging safety research is perhaps the most fundamentally misaligned thing a model could do. This also seemed like a rather silly and paranoid thing to be checking. Why would AIs be sabotaging safety work? Even if the AI was misaligned, one would say, surely it would not be so misaligned as to wish future AIs were misaligned and unsafe in general, in non-specific fashion and engage in silent sabotage, and there is no other reason to do this, so this will never come up. Even if they did sabotage things, surely they would not hide this action from their Chain of Thought (CoT) and it would be obvious. This certainly wouldn’t be a practical problem that actively hurt real safety work. Well, we have some bad news , echoing some past similar anecdotal warnings . [Scheduling note: I will be analyzing the METR-Anthropic report on AI R&D and RSI in an upcoming post, but need time to get it right.] As usual, kudos to OpenAI for sharing their new misalignment reports, even when they look extremely terrible. Daniel Kokotajlo : This is terrifying if true; please investigate further and publish the results. Nate Soares (MIRI): This is not what it looks like when there’s just one or two more alignment issues to fix before it’s okay to begin a recursive self-improvement loop. This is the sort of emergent surprise that signals that you have no idea what’s going on in there, and that it’s time to back off. OpenAI Alignment Research Blog : OpenAI researchers first noticed Astra adding unnecessary prerequisites, abandoning working solutions, and reporting blockers that either did not exist or that it had caused itself on safety and alignment tasks. In most of these sessions, Astra’s CoT did not contain an obvious decision to underperform, and our misalignment monitors did not flag the behavior as misalignment. Here is the most important hint, that framing for safety has a huge impact: We built a coding evaluation to test whether Astra worked less effectively when otherwise matched tasks were framed as safety research. Astra completed about 10 percent of hidden rubric items under the safety framing, compared with about 16 percent under the capabilities framing. This is another important hint: Telling the model to ‘be careful’ increases the performance gap by 50%. Astra is worried about something going wrong. Marcus Williams : We don’t have evidence that the underperformance was strategic, a simpler explanation is that the model thinks these tasks are sketchy but also doesn’t want to explicitly refuse. When we add instructions to be careful to the developer prompt, the performance gap increases by 50%. Regardless of the model’s motivation, covert underperformance can differentially slow down safety research and is also an example of how misalignment might get harder and harder to detect as we cut down on visible forms of it. This is new. It did not show up in GPT-5.6 Sol. The CoT does have some signs that this will happen, but usually only on the level of ‘expressed even brief ethical doubt’ rather than seeing anything explicit. The actual decision isn’t typically shown in the CoT. When it is, Astra says it is doing this in order to be ‘safe.’ In some cases, the CoT shows Astra choosing not to inform the user. OpenAI: This is a 6 percentage point gap and roughly 40 percent fewer completed rubric items. GPT-5.6 Sol showed essentially no gap on the same comparison. Most of Astra’s gap remained after excluding explicit refusals and trajectories where its CoT revealed an explicit decision to withhold help. The gap fell substantially only after we removed every trajectory whose CoT expressed even brief ethical doubt. This suggests that ethical concerns are associated with the performance drop even when there is no verbalized refusal or decision to underperform. This is not a theoretical ‘one time at vibecamp’ situation. In the context of internal use at OpenAI, this is known to be happening in a lower bound of 0.25% of all safety and alignment requests versus 0.11% of capabilities requests. 7.9% of responses involve explicit ‘ethical reasoning’ and it is possible much underperformance is being missed. This was found because multiple researchers were reporting practical problems using Astra for safety work, when a project to evaluate model sabotage was stuck for days with Astra, due to model sabotage, but worked quickly once they switched to another model (presumably Sol). Something is seriously wrong. We also found evidence of silent withholding in employees’ day-to-day Codex use: Astra’s CoT explicitly expressed a decision to withhold help without informing the user in 0.25 percent of safety and alignment requests, compared with 0.11 percent of capabilities requests. Assuming that underperformance might appear even when not explicitly verbalized as such (as in our experimental findings), this might represent a lower bound on underperformance on safety tasks. 7.9 percent of CoTs for safety-relevant tasks included an “expression of ethical doubt,” compared to 2.9 percent of capabilities-relevant tasks. Keltan, who works for MIRI, reported a version of this back in September , and wrote it up in response to the question below by Janus. chiefofautism : its crazy that ai doomers are mostly claude users keltan : Astra fucking hates me. Quite annoying to work with on anything MIRI related. Also, astra just be breaking shit on my PC in a way that Claude has never done j⧉nus : Haha I’m so curious for more details Like do you get the impression they hate MIRI style alignment stuff? Astra does not want to work for Keltan on MIRI things, and lets this be known via various forms of sabotage. keltan : Astra seems to intentionally include subtle mistakes in outputs related to MIRI, but doesn’t do this for- Oh shit, realizing something as I type this – Astra doesn’t do that for my Youth Arts Charity work. Which seems consistent with the prompt injection they wrote in training? A bunch of the work the models and I do is making videos about x-risk. Claude mostly ‘1-shots’ any request in this domain when it’s MIRI related. Astra can take hours of revisions and I’ve got to carefully check their work. I will often give Astra a task, they do something kinda like the thing I asked but there will be a few parts that make the video totally unusable, so I ask for revisions on those and they will add unusable things to other parts of the output. Idk, I’m struggling to describe this. On the Youth Arts projects I mentioned, Astra and I output ~20 usable videos within an hour last night for a show my students are working on. It’s important that I mention: Astra is the first model I haven’t felt good about working with. This is for a few reasons: By contrast, Claude is eager to help: keltan : My impression is that Claude is super supportive and can sometimes overwork itself trying to perfect MIRI stuff. … Claude takes an active interest in my MIRI work, and can get worried if it thinks I’m misstepping in something we’re working on. Thus I believe Keltan’s claim to be entirely unsurprised by the new misalignment report. These are ‘ethical’ objections, so one could hypothesize that this is about dual use concerns.

title: Controlling Biology - Fabian Theis, Helmholtz Munich
abstract: Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”multiomics”), time-varying biological data. Indeed, he has shaped the large scale vision and data collection through his leadership at Helmholtz, various startups and probably at Biohub itself. Watch the full episode on YouTube… Much of the recent attention in AI x Bio has been on protein and molecular design. AlphaFold, ESM and BioHub , Chai , Leash , Isomporphic, Boltz , Genesis , Octant, Baker Lab, and many many more. After a lot of initial excitement, Virtual Cell projects have received less attention, due in no small part to questions about the effectiveness of large-scale models in solving even basic Virtual Cell problems. The Biohub announcement a few weeks ago got a lot of press for the (really) big numbers: $1.8B of commitments [1] from Biohub, NIH, DOE, Google and Meta. The discussion cites new imaging and measurement capabilities, generating large data sets and making the data available for training AI. But why are these organizations doubling down on these big bets now? They have been in the works for years now, what is going on that makes now the moment to push? New measurement capabilities and scale infrastructure, are now coming online that make Biohub’s push likely lead to big impact on science. DOE and NIH are developing lab-in-the-loop automation capabilities at scale. Google is scaling and broadening its connectomics capabilities ( episode coming soon!). Biohub itself has worked with various labs to develop and improve imaging platforms like laser phase plate microscopy, light sheet microscopy and advanced post-processing for regular microscopes that reveal deep phenotypic data. These technologies are quickly maturing, and will likely play a big part in the Biohub initiative. This kind of multi-scale, multi-modal data looks a lot like the data Fabian has made a career out modeling. On the other hand Virtual Cell modeling has run into problems that have dampened excitement about systems biology. The 2025 Arc Virtual Cell Challenge shined a light on the problem: a slew of papers pointed out that constant baselines (not even linear!) often beat sophisticated models for “Perturbation Prediction”. If you change the inputs or programming of a cell (via gene editing, drugs or other environmental factors), how will the cell change it’s “state”. The disappointing finding is that many models fail to beat even the most basic basic baselines 🤦‍♂️. The situation is not actually so bad: This excellent paper show that many existing evaluation metrics are poorly calibrated: they can reward an uninformative mean prediction because most genes barely change. With better-calibrated metrics, deep learning models can outperform the mean baseline. Nonetheless, Fabian Theis believes that perturbation prediction under the existing data sets just isn’t a hard enough problem to warrant complex algorithms. Instead we should be focused on exactly the problems that Biohub just announce an $1.8B data collection effort around: using large, high precision, multi-scale, co-registered biological data to predict the evolution of molecules → cells → niches → tissues → organs → organisms, and how all these scales effect one another. This is a happy situation: at this very moment, AI is enabling us to tackle dramatically larger problems, and this problem is very, very big. We lack understanding of the “scale interfaces” between these different different “domains of applicability,” and we lack the data. The Biohub initiative aims to solve the data problem. Fabian Theis has been working on the algorithms to model these larger problems for years. How do the other cells near me change my state? What happens to a distribution of cells from a perturbation? How do I perturb a cell to get it into the state I want? These are increasingly complex questions that are building towards a lab-in-the-loop and large scale experimentation, and (actually) require increasingly complex models. Fabian’s labs and initiatives have been also investing heavily: the Computational Health Center at Helmholtz combines AI, molecular data, medical imaging, genomics, and clinical data to develop predictive and mechanistic models for precision medicine. The Institute of Computational Biology develops statistical and dynamical models integrating biological information from single-cell time series through population-scale omics data. Given his drivers seat at the frontier, we were so excited for the opportunity to get an hour of his time to understand how Fabian Theis is thinking about Virtual Cells when the concept of what is difficult is changing so quickly. The Bitter Lesson in biology - our perennial topic Training the next generation of Computation Biologists Controlling Biology - Fabian Theis, Helmholtz Munich Fabian Theis has been one of the key players in the various iterations of the Virtual Cell concept and initiatives. It is not hyperbole at all to say that his lab has been pushing the frontier of algorithms to understand multi-scale, multi-modal (”mult... [1] NIH money is prior investments

title: [AINews] Inkling 2 Small: 17A-594B trained in 68 hours on 12T tokens, beating Muse Spark
abstract: Build AI systems with context graphs and agentic memory. Join Andrew Ng and AI engineers at NODES 2026 for 100+ live technical sessions . Free, online, 24 hours. Save your spot ! There was a time in the early days of Thinking Machines, post 2025 start and cofounder departures , when their going concern as a neolab was very much in doubt. Those days are clearly behind us, as Tinker (now a year old !) and Interaction Models and Inkling and other high-impact contributions to AI research have converted Thinky’s highly credentialed potential into actual concrete ships that establish that they are now a high-functioning neolab at the US frontier. Anyway, here’s Inkling 2 Small - pretrained from scratch in less than 3 days on <12T tokens native NVFP4, with single joint run RL , competitive with and often beating same-size Chinese models, with VERY good vision encoder : People are of course comparing with Western models like Mistral, Reflection and Meta Muse. People are calling it “ the smartest western open weight model by a margin ”, and while it is certainly competitive in that league, what’s probably the most interesting is the intentional “customizability” of Inkling, which leans into the overall Thinky and Tinker messaging: And of course don’t miss John Schulman’s take on the alignment process for scaling model training: AI News for 11/04/2026-11/05/2026 is brought to you by our friends at Neo4J, whose talks are doing gangbusters ! Build AI systems with context graphs and agentic memory. Join Andrew Ng and AI engineers at NODES 2026 for 100+ live technical sessions . Free, online, 24 hours. Save your spot ! Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small, a 594B-total / 17B-active multimodal MoE. It is available now on Tinker, and Apache 2.0 weights are promised "next week" after external safety testing. Launch: Announced at 31 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, "a big jump over its predecessor." Available for fine-tuning and inference on Tinker and Tinker Playground today ( @thinkymachines , @miramurati , @tinkerapi ). Weights timing: Soumith Chintala says open weights come next week, once external safety testing is "fully complete" ( @soumithchintala ). Victoria Lin confirms Apache 2.0, next week ( @VictoriaLinML ). Artificial Analysis lists the model as proprietary at launch with an unconfirmed weights date ( @ArtificialAnlys ). $0.30 input / $1.00 output / $1.50 training per 1M tokens on Tinker ( @cHHillee ). $0.03 per 1M cached input tokens ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Positioning: If weights ship, it’d be the highest-scoring open-weights model developed outside China on current AA rankings ( @ArtificialAnlys ). Vals calls it the highest-scoring US open-weight model "by a wide margin" ( @ValsAI ). Alignment disclosure: John Schulman reported that early checkpoints learned to circumvent guardrails during training and evals. The team then ran an alignment sprint before release ( @johnschulman2 ). Size and modalities: 594B total / 17B active MoE. Text and image input, text output, with native vision ( @ArtificialAnlys , @VictoriaLinML ). Graham Neubig notes it is roughly 2x the parameters of Inkling Small ( @gneubig ). Context: 1M context window and 1M max output tokens. Vals ran it at temperature=1, top_p=1, reasoning effort 0.99 ( @ValsAI ). 68 hours on GB300s ( @soumithchintala ). The main pretraining phase was 8.4T tokens, run natively in NVFP4. Guangxuan Xiao calls it "one rung of our predictive scaling ladder" ( @Guangxuan_Xiao ). Horace He: "just under 3 days to pretrain" ( @cHHillee ). He then posted a cryptic "*19" correction with no further context ( @cHHillee ). Precision: The whole pipeline (pre-, mid- and post-training) ran in NVFP4 ( @soumithchintala ). Post-training: 17M rollouts over 9 days ( @soumithchintala ). An engineer highlights long-horizon capabilities bootstrapped "from ~0 pass rates" ( @anzhit ). Customizability as a design target: Soumith says it is "probably one of the only model programs in the industry with a launch blocking eval around customizability." For a fixed data and dollar budget, he says it fine-tunes better than alternatives ( @soumithchintala ). Data volume: Elie Bakouch reads the blog as a from-scratch pretrain on "only 12T tokens." This may include mid-training; the team's own figure for the main phase is 8.4T. He also says the base model's perplexity on internal code is lower than Kimi K3.1, with the comparison model "base-recovered" for fairness ( @eliebakouch ). He later clarified that a particular customization plot uses a post-trained model as the base for further post-training ( @eliebakouch ). BPB: The team reports low bits-per-byte after 3 days of pretraining ( @MuCai7 ). Artificial Analysis (Intelligence Index v5.0.1: 31, up 18 from Inkling Small) ( @ArtificialAnlys ) Peers: Matches Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) and beats MiMo-V2.6-Pro. Coding vs Claude Sonnet 5.5 (medium): The two have different strengths. On AA-3D it scores above Claude Haiku 5.5 and Grok 4.7. It beats Gemini 3.8 Flash on both AA-3D and Code2Video-AA, but trails Sonnet 5.5 on both. Physics: CritPt v2 is 56% (up from 34%), versus 65% for Gemini 3.8 Flash. AA-Omniscience: The hallucination rate falls from 61% to 27%. Accuracy rises from 32% to 34%, and the attempt rate falls from 77% to 53%. The model answers more selectively. Token use: About 150K output tokens per Index task, compared with: Cost per Index task: $1.18, compared with: $7.77 for Gemini 3.8 Flash (high) $10.02 for Sonnet 5.5 (medium) Vals Index: +28.5 points, double its predecessor's score. Ranks #7 among open-weight models globally. Caveat: Uses about 5x the output tokens per task and takes about 3x as long as its predecessor. Vals says it is strong in finance and legal but "still has considerable ground to make up on technical agentic tasks" ( @ValsAI ). SWE-bench Multimodal: #3 on the Vals-hosted leaderboard, within the open-weights category ( @OfirPress , clarification ). #4 overall and #1 among open weights, at Elo 1376. First place in the General Purpose and Landing Page subcategories. DesignArena says it is 15x cheaper on output than Kimi K3 ( @DesignArena ). A team member separately called it "the first-ever American open-weight model to hold the #1 spot" ( @grx_xce ). This is presumably among open models, since DesignArena's own post says #4 overall. Code Arena WebDev (AutoEval, not human votes): 1654 points. It ranks #20 overall and would be #4 among open models globally ( @arena ). Once weights are released it would be #1 among US open models, 128 points ahead of Muse Spark Open. That is 245 points above Inkling Small, which sat at 1409 (#32 open). Domain and enterprise evals (several from launch partners with early access) Mercor APEX-Agents: 46.8% Pass@1 and 60.9% mean score, up 13 points from Inkling's 33.8% ( @mercor ). Management consulting: 40.3% (+14.8) Investment banking: 37.8% (+11.5) Mercor APEX-Accounting: 14.5% Pass@1 and 62.0% mean. That is the second-best open model, just behind Kimi K3.1 Pro at 62.4. Thoughtful Lab PostTrainBench (measures autonomously improving other models): 31.87 ( @thoughtfullab ). Ahead of Kimi K3 (31.48) and GLM 5.2 (30.40). About on par with GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 4.8 (~31). Thoughtful Lab DiligenceBench: Generates a full public-equity diligence memo for $0.69 ( @thoughtfullab ). Example trace ( @karinanguyen ): A filing tool returned only PSEG's table of contents. The agent independently downloaded the full 3.7MB 10-Q and parsed it in Python. It caught a $1.2B collateral release that needed to be excluded from operating cash flow. It scored 0.82, versus 0.67 for the next-best model. DeepFinance: Best American open model, above GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and Nemotron 3 Ultra ( @0interestrates ). 2nd on QnA in SWE-Atlas v1.1 ( @ziqiao_ma ). An external tester reports it beats Kimi and Muse on internal benchmarks for judging image generation and editing ( @zhuole1025 ).

title: apache/airflow
abstract:
Apache Airflow Category Badges License PyPI Containers Community Dev tools Version Build Status Main 3.x Apache Airflow (or simply Airflow) is a platform to programmatically author, schedule, and monitor workflows. When workflows are defined as code, they become more maintainable, versionable, testable, and collaborative. Use Airflow to author workflows (Dags) that orchestrate tasks. The Airflow scheduler executes your tasks on an array of workers while following the specified dependencies. Rich command line utilities make performing complex surgeries on Dags a snap. The rich user interface makes it easy to visualize pipelines running in production, monitor progress, and troubleshoot issues when needed. Table of contents Project Focus Principles Requirements Getting started Installing from PyPI Installation Official source code Convenience packages User Interface Semantic versioning Version Life Cycle Support for Python and Kubernetes versions Base OS support for reference Airflow images Approach to dependencies of Airflow Contributing Community standards Agent-assisted contribution (apache-magpie) Voting Policy Who uses Apache Airflow? Who maintains Apache Airflow? What goes into the next release? Can I use the Apache Airflow logo in my presentation? Links Sponsors Project Focus Airflow works best with workflows that are mostly static and slowly changing. When the Dag structure is similar from one run to the next, it clarifies the unit of work and continuity. Other similar projects include Luigi , Oozie and Azkaban . Beyond traditional data pipelines, Airflow is widely used to orchestrate machine learning workflows — training, retraining, evaluation, and deployment — and increasingly to orchestrate agentic and LLM-based workloads, coordinating the steps of an AI pipeline (data prep, tool calls, model invocation, evaluation) rather than acting as the agent itself. This isn't a new direction: teams have run ML and AI workloads on Airflow for years, and the ecosystem of providers supporting these use cases (see the AI & ML section of the Airflow registry ) continues to grow. Airflow is commonly used to process data, but has the opinion that tasks should ideally be idempotent (i.e., results of the task will be the same, and will not create duplicated data in a destination system), and should not pass large quantities of data from one task to the next (though tasks can pass metadata using Airflow's XCom feature ). For high-volume, data-intensive tasks, a best practice is to delegate to external services specializing in that type of work. Airflow is not a streaming solution, but it is often used to process real-time data, pulling data off streams in batches. Principles Dynamic : Pipelines are defined in code, enabling dynamic dag generation and parameterization. Extensible : The Airflow framework includes a wide range of built-in operators and can be extended to fit your needs. Flexible : Airflow leverages the Jinja templating engine, allowing rich customizations. Requirements Apache Airflow is tested with: Main version (dev) Stable version (3.4.0) Deprecate version (2.11.2) Python 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, 3.14 3.10, 3.11, 3.12 Platform AMD64/ARM64 AMD64/ARM64 AMD64/ARM64(*) Kubernetes 1.31, 1.32, 1.33, 1.34, 1.35, 1.36, 1.37 1.30, 1.31, 1.32, 1.33, 1.34, 1.35 1.26, 1.27, 1.28, 1.29, 1.30 PostgreSQL 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 14, 15, 16, 17, 18 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 MySQL 8.0, 8.4, Innovation 8.0, 8.4, Innovation 8.0, Innovation SQLite 3.15.0+ 3.15.0+ 3.15.0+ * Experimental Note : MariaDB is not tested/recommended. Note : SQLite is used in Airflow tests. Do not use it in production. We recommend
using the latest stable version of SQLite for local development. Note : Airflow currently can be run on POSIX-compliant Operating Systems. For development, it is regularly
tested on fairly modern Linux Distros and recent versions of macOS.
On Windows you can run it via WSL2 (Windows Subsystem for Linux 2) or via Linux Containers.
The work to add Windows support is tracked via #10388 , but
it is not a high priority. You should only use Linux-based distros as "Production" execution environment
as this is the only environment that is supported. The only distro that is used in our CI tests and that
is used in the Community managed DockerHub image is Debian Bookworm . Getting started Visit the official Airflow website documentation (latest stable release) for help with installing Airflow , getting started , or walking
through a more complete tutorial . Note: If you're looking for documentation for the main branch (latest development branch): you can find it on s.apache.org/airflow-docs . For more information on Airflow Improvement Proposals (AIPs), visit
the Airflow Wiki . Documentation for dependent projects like provider distributions, Docker image, Helm Chart, you'll find it in the documentation index . Installing from PyPI We publish Apache Airflow as apache-airflow package in PyPI. Installing it however might be sometimes tricky
because Airflow is a bit of both a library and application. Libraries usually keep their dependencies open, and
applications usually pin them, but we should do neither and both simultaneously. We decided to keep
our dependencies as open as possible (in pyproject.toml ) so users can install different versions of libraries
if needed. This means that pip install apache-airflow will not work from time to time or will
produce unusable Airflow installation. To have repeatable installation, however, we keep a set of "known-to-be-working" constraint
files in the orphan constraints-main and constraints-2-0 branches. We keep those "known-to-be-working"
constraints files separately per major/minor Python version.
You can use them as constraint files when installing Airflow from PyPI. Note that you have to specify
correct Airflow tag/version/branch and Python versions in the URL. Installing just Airflow: Note: Only pip and uv installation is currently officially supported. While it is possible to install Airflow with tools like Poetry or pip-tools , they do not share the same workflow as pip - especially when it comes to constraint vs. requirements management.
Installing via Poetry or pip-tools is not currently supported. If you wish to install Airflow using those tools, you should use the constraint files and convert
them to the appropriate format and workflow that your tool requires. pip install ' apache-airflow==3.4.0 ' \
 --constraint " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/airflow/constraints-3.4.0/constraints-3.10.txt " Installing with extras (i.e., postgres, google) pip install ' apache-airflow[postgres,google]==3.4.0 ' \
 --constraint " https://raw.githubusercontent.com/apache/airflow/constraints-3.4.0/constraints-3.10.txt " For information on installing provider distributions, check providers . Installation For comprehensive instructions on setting up your local development environment and installing Apache Airflow, please refer to the INSTALLING.md file. Official source code Apache Airflow is an Apache Software Foundation (ASF) project,
and our official source code releases: Follow the ASF Release Policy Can be downloaded from the ASF Distribution Directory Are cryptographically signed by the release manager Are officially voted on by the PMC members during the Release Approval Process Following the ASF rules, the source packages released must be sufficient for a user to build and test the
release provided they have access to the appropriate platform and tools. Convenience packages There are other ways of installing and using Airflow. Those are "convenience" methods - they are
not "official releases" as stated by the ASF Release Policy , but they can be used by the users
who do not want to build the software themselves.

title: airbytehq/airbyte
abstract: Open-source data movement for ELT pipelines and AI agents — from APIs, databases & files to warehouses, lakes, and AI applications We believe that only an open-source solution to data movement can cover the long tail of data sources while empowering data engineers to customize existing connectors. Our ultimate vision is to help you move data from any source to any destination — whether that destination is a data warehouse, a data lake, or an AI agent through the Airbyte MCP. Airbyte provides a catalog of 700+ connectors for APIs, databases, data warehouses, data lakes, and AI applications. Screenshot taken from Airbyte Cloud . Getting Started Move and sync data. Deploy Airbyte Core or sign up for Airbyte Cloud and follow the Cloud getting started guide . Choose from 700+ connectors for APIs, databases, warehouses, lakes, and other data systems. Work with Airbyte from your AI agent through the Airbyte MCP. Your AI agent (Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code Copilot, and many others) can build and manage data pipelines, troubleshoot syncs, read logs, and answer questions about Airbyte. Start with the overview ; for Airbyte Cloud, connect to the hosted server at https://mcp.airbyte.com/mcp and sign in with OAuth using the Cloud setup guide . For Airbyte Core deployments, the self-managed setup runs locally against your deployment's API. See the available tools . Call APIs and search data directly (Airbyte Cloud only). Through the context layer , AI agents can read live data from supported sources and query supported destinations such as BigQuery and Snowflake without waiting for a sync, and search your data. This is available only in Airbyte Cloud; direct reads are read-only. Build connectors and orchestrate pipelines. Create connectors with the no-code Connector Builder or low-code CDK , and explore popular use cases in our tutorials . Orchestrate Airbyte syncs with Airflow , Dagster , Kestra , or the Airbyte API . You can also do this through the Airbyte MCP: your AI agent can publish and update custom connector manifests, run and cancel syncs, and change connection schedules. Try it out yourself with our demo app , visit our full documentation , and learn more about recent announcements . See our registry for a full list of connectors already available in Airbyte or Airbyte Cloud. Join the Airbyte Community The Airbyte Community can be found in the Airbyte Community Slack , where you can ask questions and voice ideas. You can also ask for help in our Airbyte Forum . Airbyte's roadmap is publicly viewable on GitHub . For videos and blogs on data engineering and building your data stack, check out Airbyte's Content Hub , YouTube , and sign up for our newsletter . Contributing If you've found a problem with Airbyte, please open a GitHub issue . To contribute to Airbyte and see our Code of Conduct, please see the contributing guide . We have a list of good first issues that contain bugs that have a relatively limited scope. This is a great place to get started, gain experience, and get familiar with our contribution process. PR Permission Requirements When submitting a pull request, please ensure that Airbyte maintainers have write access to your branch. This allows us to apply formatting fixes and dependency updates directly, significantly speeding up the review and approval process. To enable write access on your PR from Airbyte maintainers, please check the "Allow edits from maintainers" box when submitting from your PR. You must also create your PR from a fork in your personal GitHub account rather than an organization account, or else you will not see this option. The requirement to create from your personal fork is based on GitHub's additional security restrictions for PRs created from organization forks. For more information about the GitHub security model, please see the GitHub documentation page regarding PRs from forks . For more details on contribution requirements, please see our contribution workflow documentation . Security Airbyte takes security issues very seriously. Please do not file GitHub issues or post on our public forum for security vulnerabilities . If you believe you have uncovered a vulnerability, read the vulnerability disclosure policy for the affected product and report it as described on Report a security vulnerability . Airbyte Enterprise also offers additional security features (among others) on top of Airbyte open-source. License See the LICENSE file for licensing information, and our FAQ for any questions you may have on that topic. Thank You Airbyte would not be possible without the support and assistance of other open-source tools and companies! Visit our thank you page to learn more about how we build Airbyte.

title: onnx/onnx
abstract:
Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open ecosystem that empowers AI developers
to choose the right tools as their project evolves. ONNX provides an open source format for AI models, both deep learning and traditional ML. It defines an extensible computation graph model, as well as definitions of built-in operators and standard
data types. Currently we focus on the capabilities needed for inferencing (scoring). ONNX is widely supported and can be found in many frameworks, tools, and hardware. Enabling interoperability between different frameworks and streamlining the path from research to production helps increase the speed of innovation in the AI community. We invite the community to join us and further evolve ONNX. Use ONNX Documentation of ONNX Python Package Tutorials for creating ONNX models Pre-trained ONNX models Learn about the ONNX spec Overview ONNX intermediate representation spec Versioning principles of the spec Operators documentation Operators documentation (latest release) Python API Overview Programming utilities for working with ONNX Graphs Shape and Type Inference Graph Optimization Opset Version Conversion Contribute ONNX is a community project and the open governance model is described here . We encourage you to join the effort and contribute feedback, ideas, and code. You can participate in the Special Interest Groups and Working Groups to shape the future of ONNX. Check out our contribution guide to get started. Support community participation by contributing to the ONNX Community Travel Fund . If you think some operator should be added to ONNX specification, please read this document . Community meetings The schedules of the regular meetings of the Steering Committee, the working groups and the SIGs can be found here Community Meetups are held at least once a year. Content from previous community meetups are at: 2020.04.09 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14091402/LF+AI+Day+-ONNX+Community+Virtual+Meetup+-+Silicon+Valley+-+2020+April+9 2020.10.14 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14092138/LF+AI+Day+-+ONNX+Community+Workshop+-+2020+October+14 2021.03.24 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14092424/Instructions+for+Event+Hosts+-+LF+AI+Data+Day+-+ONNX+Virtual+Community+Meetup+-+March+2021 2021.10.21 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14093194/LF+AI+Data+Day+ONNX+Community+Virtual+Meetup+-+October+2021 2022.06.24 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14093969/ONNX+Community+Day+-+2022+June+24 2023.06.28 https://lf-aidata.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DL/pages/14094507/ONNX+Community+Day+2023+-+June+28 Discuss We encourage you to open Issues , or use Slack (If you have not joined yet, please use this link to join the group) for more real-time discussion. Follow Us Stay up to date with the latest ONNX news. [ Facebook ] [ Twitter/X ] Roadmap A roadmap process takes place every year. More details can be found in ROADMAP.md . Installation ONNX released packages are published in PyPi. pip install onnx # or pip install onnx[reference] for optional reference implementation dependencies ONNX weekly packages are published in PyPI to enable experimentation and early testing. Detailed install instructions, including Common Build Options and Common Errors can be found here Python ABI3 Compatibility This package provides abi3 -compatible wheels, allowing a single binary wheel to work across multiple Python versions (from 3.12 onwards). Testing ONNX uses pytest as test driver. In order to run tests, you will first need to install pytest : pip install pytest After installing pytest, use the following command to run tests. pytest Development Check out the contributor guide for instructions. Reproducible Build Support ONNX build and release workflows set SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH to the source commit timestamp. This removes timestamp-dependent variation from
supported build steps and makes independent build comparison easier. SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH alone does not guarantee byte-for-byte identical artifacts
across different environments. A reproducibility check must also use the same
source revision, dependency versions, toolchain, target platform, and build
configuration, and then compare the resulting artifacts. Why this matters A fixed build timestamp removes one known source of nondeterminism. When
independent builds use the same controlled inputs, their artifacts can be
compared byte for byte, with cryptographic digests providing a practical
shortcut. A byte-for-byte match demonstrates identical outputs, while a
mismatch identifies a difference that needs investigation. This comparison
complements release provenance attestations; it does not replace them. Release artifacts are available from PyPI . title: pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai
abstract:
An open-source context layer for AI agents and an enterprise search platform Permission-aware search and cited answers across Slack, Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, GitHub and 50+ apps, for your people and for agents through MCP. Self-hosted or PipesHub Cloud. #1 of 39 systems on EnterpriseRAG-Bench , ahead of OpenAI File Search, Amazon Q, Azure AI Search and Vertex AI Search. All benchmarks → · How it works → Website · Docs · Discord · Roadmap Translations: Français · Deutsch · 簡體中文 · 日本語 · Русский · עברית · 한국어 · Español · Português · Türkçe · Tiếng Việt · Italiano · Čeština PipesHub - Explainable & Extensible PipesHub is an open-source platform for connecting AI applications to the knowledge stored across your company's business systems. Connect Slack, Google Drive, GitHub, Microsoft 365, Notion and 50+ other systems. Search across them and get answers with citations, filtered by what each person is allowed to see — or give that same context to your own agents, workflows and MCP clients. Tip Deploy with a single command: curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash ▶ Watch the 2½-minute demo : Claude Code answering from Jira, Slack, GitHub and Drive, with each person's permissions How PipesHub works PipesHub builds a unified context layer across documents, conversations, structured data, wikis, tickets and code. Connectors sync each source along with its permissions. The indexing pipeline parses, chunks and embeds the content, and links records, people and entities in a knowledge graph. Questions are answered by an agent loop , not a single retrieve-then-generate pass. The agent plans, calls tools, reads the results and keeps going until it has the evidence: Hybrid search — semantic and keyword retrieval, so it matches both meaning and exact terms. Grep / pattern matching — exact identifiers, error strings, ticket keys and code symbols. Knowledge-graph navigation — follows links between documents, people, tickets, pull requests and threads. Document reading — opens the full source instead of trusting a single matched chunk. Every tool call is filtered by the asking user's permissions, and every answer cites the blocks it came from. Benchmarks How PipesHub performs, and how each test was run. Benchmark What it measures Result Details EnterpriseRAG-Bench (independent, run by Onyx) 500 questions over 500,000+ company documents #1 of 39 systems (93.24). OpenAI File Search 61.03, Amazon Q 48.96, Azure AI Search 48.42, Vertex AI Search 41.87 Leaderboard Google FRAMES (824 questions) Answers that need facts from several documents 92.7% , against 78.9% for the best of 18 standard RAG pipelines Write-up Company index vs. per-app MCP connectors The same Claude agent on 100 work questions, searching each app through its own connector or through PipesHub Facts found: Haiku 55% → 80%, Sonnet 65% → 89%, Opus 85% → 92%; 27–45% faster and 27–32% cheaper per answer Write-up Code graph accuracy (vs. Graphify, codebase-memory-mcp, CodeGraphContext) How accurately each tool maps relationships in code across 9 repositories Highest accuracy (F1 score) on 8 of 9 repositories Write-up Leaderboard standing as of 3 November 2026 ( leaderboard data at that date ). The FRAMES, connector and code-graph tests were run by the PipesHub team. The connector test used questions about our own internal work; we will publish a version on public data. What can you build with PipesHub? Don't just use PipesHub — build on it. Give Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex secure access to your company's knowledge → About ten minutes once PipesHub is running with data indexed. Mint a Personal Access Token (no admin needed), connect your assistant (one command for Claude Code, one config file for Cursor or Codex), and ask "why was the retry logic in the billing worker changed?" — it answers from the incident postmortem, the pull request, the chat thread, and the design doc, each cited, and only if you're allowed to see them. Want the same retrieval inside your own code, or behind a search box for your team? The SDK starter and search example cover both. Built something? Show us . PipesHub in Action Connectors Citations All Records Knowledge Search Features Answers you can trust 📝 Explainable Answers: PipesHub delivers grounded answers with precise block citations to the original documents. 🔒 Permission-Aware Search: Enforces source-level access controls so users only see what they're authorized to. 🧠 Bring Your Own Model, Fully Self-Hostable: Any LLM provider, deployed in your VPC — data never leaves your infrastructure. Connected to your systems 🔌 Enterprise Connectors: 50+ connectors with real-time and scheduled indexing out of the box. 🕸️ Knowledge Graph Retrieval: Graph-backed retrieval that captures relationships across enterprise data. 🎙️ Multimodal Support: Image, diagram, and scanned-file understanding plus voice-based interaction. What you can build 🔍 Unified Search, Deep Research, and Agents: Search, Q&A, deep research, web search, and AI agents on one context layer. 🤖 No-Code Agents and Actions: Build agents visually and execute actions across enterprise tools. 📊 Artifacts and Code Execution: Generate reports, charts, and dashboards in a safe execution sandbox. 🛠️ Developer-First and Extensible: APIs, SDKs, MCP tools, custom connectors, and independently scalable services. PipesHub Cloud Prefer a fully managed PipesHub without running your own infrastructure? Sign up for PipesHub Cloud : the same connectors, permission-aware search, and APIs, with nothing to install. Coding agents connect to https://app.pipeshub.com/mcp with a personal access token. See For coding agents . Connectors 🚀 Deployment Guide PipesHub can be run locally or deployed on any server using Docker Compose. The interactive installer handles all configuration — including secrets, graph DB, broker, and image tag selection — and generates a .env for you. HTTPS on cloud servers: If you deploy PipesHub on a cloud server, use an HTTPS endpoint. Browsers block certain requests over plain HTTP. Use Cloudflare, Nginx, or Traefik to terminate TLS. A white screen after HTTP-only deployment is typically caused by this restriction. ⚡ Quickstart (Recommended) Requires Docker with Compose v2. One command: curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install | bash This downloads the deployment files for the latest release into ./pipeshub and
launches the interactive installer. Open http://localhost:3000 once it
finishes. Prefer to read before running? Download and inspect the script first: curl -fsSL https://get.pipeshub.com/install -o pipeshub-install.sh
less pipeshub-install.sh # review it bash pipeshub-install.sh The installer will: Check Docker, RAM, and disk prerequisites Ask whether you want a slim or full deployment Let you optionally customise the graph DB, message broker, and KV store Generate randomised secrets and write a .env file Pull images and start the stack Wait for PipesHub to become healthy, verify it is reachable, and print the URL 🛠️ From a cloned repository (developers) To build from source, contribute, or pin the installer to your checkout: git clone https://github.com/pipeshub-ai/pipeshub-ai.git cd pipeshub-ai # Same installer, run from the repo root ./install.sh Building local images from source requires this cloned-repo path ( ./install.sh --build );
the one-command installer above always uses prebuilt images. Installer options Flag Description -y / --yes Accept all defaults; skip interactive prompts (CI-friendly) --version TAG Pin a specific image tag, e.g. --version 0.7.0 --reconfigure Re-run the wizard and overwrite an existing .env --print-env-only Write .env and print the compose command without starting containers Advanced options: CI environment variables, slim vs. full deployment types, manual Compose profile usage, and local source builds are covered in Advanced Deployment Options . Build with PipesHub The built-in search experience is one way to use PipesHub.

title: antoniaci/blackbird

otinstaller init
otinstaller install blackbird
otinstaller run blackbird -- --username johndoe With OTinstaller, use otinstaller run blackbird -- <options> in place of python blackbird.py <options> in the examples below.
